claim: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control multiple aspects of post-transcriptional gene regulation and function during various biological processes in the nervous system.
source: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control multiple aspects of post-transcriptional gene regulation and function during various biological processes in the nervous system.
evidence: This is a general statement about RBPs supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The NOVA family of RBPs play a key role in neuronal migration, axon outgrowth, and axon guidance.
source: We found that the NOVA family of RBPs play a key role in neuronal migration, axon outgrowth, and axon guidance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the RNAi screen and phenotypic analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nova mutants display similar defects as the knockout of the Dcc transmembrane receptor.
source: Interestingly, Nova mutants display similar defects as the knockout of the Dcc transmembrane receptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative phenotypic data shown in Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6.

claim: Nova deficiency disrupts the alternative splicing of Dcc.
source: We show here that Nova deficiency disrupts the alternative splicing of Dcc
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Restoring Dcc splicing in Nova knockouts is able to rescue the defects.
source: and that restoring Dcc splicing in Nova knockouts is able to rescue the defects.
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The production of DCC splice variants controlled by NOVA has a crucial function during many stages of commissural neuron development.
source: Together, our results demonstrate that the production of DCC splice variants controlled by NOVA has a crucial function during many stages of commissural neuron development.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined data from splicing assays, rescue experiments, and phenotypic analyses throughout the manuscript.

claim: Alternative splicing generates gene function complexity in many neural developmental processes, including neuronal differentiation, neuronal migration, axon growth and guidance, and synapse formation and function.
source: Alternative splicing generates gene function complexity in many neural developmental processes, including neuronal differentiation, neuronal migration, axon growth and guidance, and synapse formation and function (Grabowski and Black, 2001; Lee and Irizarry, 2003; Li et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A large number of axon guidance molecules undergo alternative splicing, including Dscam.
source: A large number of axon guidance molecules undergo alternative splicing, including Dscam (Schmucker et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Netrin ligands and their Dcc and Neogenin receptors undergo alternative splicing.
source: Netrin ligands and their Dcc and Neogenin receptors (Keeling et al., 1997; Reale et al., 1994; Zhang et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Slit ligands and Robo receptors undergo alternative splicing.
source: Slit ligands and Robo receptors (Camurri et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2008; Clark et al., 2002; Dalkic et al., 2006; Little et al., 2002; Tanno et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Semaphorin ligands and Neuropilin and Plexin receptors undergo alternative splicing.
source: Semaphorin ligands and Neuropilin and Plexin receptors (Cackowski et al., 2004; Correa et al., 2001; Qu et al., 2002; Takahashi et al., 2009; Tamagnone et al., 1999)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ephrins and Ephs undergo alternative splicing.
source: and Ephrins and Ephs (Holmberg et al., 2000; Lai et al., 1999; Sajjadi et al., 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The functional significance of alternative splicing events in axon guidance molecules and the splicing factors responsible for generating protein variants remain largely uncharacterized.
source: However, the functional significance of these alternative splicing events and the splicing factors responsible for generating protein variants for these molecules remain largely uncharacterized.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' assessment of the state of the field.

claim: Netrin and Dcc function during cell migration, neurite specification and growth, axon guidance, synaptogenesis, and tumorigenesis.
source: Netrin and Dcc (deleted in colorectal carcinoma) function during cell migration, neurite specification and growth, axon guidance, synaptogenesis, and tumorigenesis (Cooper et al., 1999; Killeen, 2009; Mehlen and Tauszig-Delamasure, 2014; Moore et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Within the spinal cord commissural neurons, DCC is required for Netrin-stimulated axon outgrowth.
source: Within the spinal cord commissural neurons, DCC is required for Netrin-stimulated axon outgrowth and for attracting the axons to the Netrin-secreting midline (Dickson, 2002; Dickson and Zou, 2010; Evans and Bashaw, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DCC is required for attracting commissural axons to the Netrin-secreting midline.
source: Within the spinal cord commissural neurons, DCC is required for Netrin-stimulated axon outgrowth and for attracting the axons to the Netrin-secreting midline (Dickson, 2002; Dickson and Zou, 2010; Evans and Bashaw, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mammalian Dcc undergoes alternative splicing to generate two isoforms that differ in the extracellular domain, in the linker sequence between the fourth and fifth fibronectin repeats (FN4 and FN5).
source: Mammalian Dcc undergoes alternative splicing to generate two isoforms that differ in the extracellular domain, in the linker sequence between the fourth and fifth fibronectin repeats (FN4 and FN5) (Reale et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Dcc alternative splicing was first reported in neuroblastoma cells and was found to be disrupted in these tumor cells.
source: This alternative splicing was first reported in neuroblastoma cells and was found to be disrupted in these tumor cells (Reale et al., 1994)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The physiological significance of Dcc alternative splicing was completely unknown.
source: but its physiological significance was completely unknown.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' assessment of the state of the field prior to their study.

claim: DCClong contains extra 20 amino acids in the FN4-FN5 linker.
source: We refer to the splice variants hereafter as DCClong and DCCshort, with DCClong containing extra 20 amino acids in the FN4-FN5 linker.
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on the known structure of the protein.

claim: The two DCC isoforms bind Netrin-1 with comparable affinities.
source: Interestingly, a recent structure study shows that the two isoforms bind Netrin-1 with comparable affinities, but are likely to adopt distinct conformations upon ligand binding (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The two DCC isoforms are likely to adopt distinct conformations upon ligand binding.
source: Interestingly, a recent structure study shows that the two isoforms bind Netrin-1 with comparable affinities, but are likely to adopt distinct conformations upon ligand binding (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Nova1 and Nova2 knockdown leads to severe defects in the dorsal spinal cord interneurons, including the commissural interneurons.
source: we carried out an in vivo RNAi screen against candidate RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) in cultured mouse embryos, and found that Nova1 and Nova2 knockdown leads to severe defects in the dorsal spinal cord interneurons, including the commissural interneurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1.

claim: The NOVA proteins were first identified as the autoimmune antigens in the neurodegenerative disease POMA (paraneoplastic opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia).
source: The NOVA (neuro-oncological ventral antigen) proteins were first identified as the autoimmune antigens in the neurodegenerative disease POMA (paraneoplastic opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia; Darnell, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: NOVA1/2 are neural-specific KH (hnRNP K homology)-type of RBPs that can directly regulate alternative splicing.
source: NOVA1/2 are neural-specific KH (hnRNP K homology)-type of RBPs that can directly regulate alternative splicing (Buckanovich et al., 1996; Lewis et al., 1999; Ule et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Genome-wide studies have identified many potential NOVA targets that are involved in various neural developmental processes.
source: Genome-wide studies have identified many potential NOVA targets that are involved in various neural developmental processes (Licatalosi et al., 2008; Ule et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In vivo studies using Nova knockout mice have demonstrated defects in synapse formation and function, and in neuronal migration.
source: In vivo studies using Nova knockout mice have demonstrated defects in synapse formation and function, and in neuronal migration (Huang et al., 2005; Jensen et al., 2000; Ruggiu et al., 2009; Yano et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nova1/2 loss of function reduces the migration of the spinal cord interneurons and their progenitors.
source: We show here that Nova1/2 loss of function reduces the migration of the spinal cord interneurons and their progenitors
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Nova1/2 loss of function disturbs the axon outgrowth and guidance of the commissural interneurons.
source: and disturbs the axon outgrowth and guidance of the commissural interneurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Nova defects resemble those seen in Dcc knockouts.
source: Interestingly, these defects resemble those seen in Dcc knockouts.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative phenotypic data shown in Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6.

claim: Dcc alternative splicing is perturbed by Nova deficiency in vivo.
source: Consistently, Dcc alternative splicing is perturbed by Nova deficiency in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Restoring Dcclong, the diminished isoform in Nova knockouts, is able to reverse the defects.
source: Through rescue experiments, we show that restoring Dcclong, the diminished isoform in Nova knockouts, is able to reverse the defects.
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: NOVA1/2 regulate Dcc pre-mRNA splicing in in vitro assays.
source: Furthermore, NOVA1/2 regulate Dcc pre-mRNA splicing in in vitro assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by splicing assay data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Dcc alternative splicing is important for the gene function and is controlled by the NOVA splicing factors.
source: Together, our results demonstrate that Dcc alternative splicing is important for the gene function and is controlled by the NOVA splicing factors.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined data from splicing assays, rescue experiments, and phenotypic analyses throughout the manuscript.

claim: The dorsal interneuron progenitors are mostly targeted by electroporation, whereas the ventral motor neuron progenitors are not.
source: We observed that the dorsal interneuron progenitors are mostly targeted, whereas the ventral motor neuron progenitors are not (Chen et al., 2008; Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation and citation to previous work, with visual evidence in Figure 1B.

claim: The dorsal progenitors are more actively proliferating and differentiating during the culture period.
source: This is likely due to the fact that the dorsal progenitors are more actively proliferating and differentiating during the culture period.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed targeting pattern.

claim: Actb-gfp was used to label the highly heterogeneous populations of commissural neurons.
source: We used Actb-gfp (aka βactin-gfp) in order to label the highly heterogeneous populations of commissural neurons, which are mostly descended from the dorsal progenitors.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental approach.

claim: Following electroporation, the mitotic neuroprogenitors migrate laterally away from the ventricle.
source: Following electroporation, the mitotic neuroprogenitors migrate laterally away from the ventricle (Caspary and Anderson, 2003; Helms and Johnson, 2003; Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Upon neural differentiation around E10 in mice, the progenitors exit the cell cycle and migrate out of the ventricular zone (VZ) to reach the lateral spinal cord.
source: Upon neural differentiation around E10 in mice, the progenitors exit the cell cycle and migrate out of the ventricular zone (VZ) to reach the lateral spinal cord.
evidence: This is a statement about known developmental processes.

claim: Differentiated interneurons, including commissural and ipsilateral-projecting neurons continue to migrate laterally and different subpopulations also migrate dorsally or ventrally to reach their final positions.
source: Differentiated interneurons, including commissural and ipsilateral-projecting neurons continue to migrate laterally and different subpopulations also migrate dorsally or ventrally to reach their final positions.
evidence: This is a statement about known developmental processes, supported by citation.

claim: Mature commissural neurons grow out axons and project them toward and across the ventral midline.
source: Mature commissural neurons then grow out axons and project them toward and across the ventral midline (Caspary and Anderson, 2003; Helms and Johnson, 2003; Lu et al., 2015; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Nova and Dcc deficiency leads to an increased number of neuroprogenitors in the VZ.
source: Nova and Dcc deficiency leads to an increased number of neuroprogenitors in the VZ (asterisk)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: Nova and Dcc deficiency leads to fewer and shorter ventrally-projecting axons.
source: and fewer and shorter ventrally-projecting axons (arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: Single knockdown of either Nova1 or Nova2 had no effect compared with control siRNAs.
source: We found that single knockdown of either Nova1 or Nova2 had no effect compared with control siRNAs
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the RNAi screen.

claim: A pan-Nova siRNA that targets both homologues caused severe defects.
source: but a pan-Nova siRNA that targets both homologues caused severe defects (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Neither Nova1 nor Nova2 single KOs displayed any defect.
source: We found that neither Nova1 nor Nova2 single KOs displayed any defect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from knockout mice.

claim: Nova1 KO; Nova2 KO (Nova dKO) caused the same defects as Nova1/2 double knockdown.
source: However, Nova1 KO; Nova2 KO (referred to hereafter as Nova dKO) caused the same defects as Nova1/2 double knockdown (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Nova1 Het; Nova2 KO displayed the same defects as Nova dKO.
source: In addition, Nova1 Het; Nova2 KO displayed the same defects
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Other genotype combinations including Nova1 KO; Nova2 Het are phenotypically normal.
source: whereas other genotype combinations including Nova1 KO; Nova2 Het are phenotypically normal (see below).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown later in the manuscript.

claim: Nova1 and Nova2 have redundant functions in regulating dorsal interneuron development.
source: Thus, Nova1 and Nova2 have redundant functions in regulating dorsal interneuron development
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic data showing that both genes need to be disrupted to see a phenotype.

claim: Nova2 appears to play a major role in regulating dorsal interneuron development.
source: and Nova2 appears to play a major role.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Nova1 Het; Nova2 KO shows defects while Nova1 KO; Nova2 Het does not.

claim: The Netrin-DCC signaling is required to stimulate commissural axon outgrowth and to attract the axons to the ventral midline.
source: The Netrin-DCC signaling is required to stimulate commissural axon outgrowth and to attract the axons to the ventral midline
evidence: This is a statement about known signaling pathways in the field.

claim: Dcc KOs display the same defects as Nova dKOs, namely more GFP+ neurons within the VZ, and shorter and fewer ventrally projecting axons.
source: Interestingly, we observed the same defects in Dcc KOs, namely more GFP+ neurons within the VZ, and shorter and fewer ventrally projecting axons (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Nova and Dcc KOs labeled with Atoh1-gfp show a reduction in axon ventral projection.
source: We also labeled Nova and Dcc KOs with Atoh1-gfp (aka Math1-gfp), which is expressed in the dorsal most dI1 subpopulation of interneurons and their progenitors (Lumpkin et al., 2003). Similarly, we observed a reduction in axon ventral projection in both mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Atoh1-gfp is expressed in the dorsal most dI1 subpopulation of interneurons and their progenitors.
source: We also labeled Nova and Dcc KOs with Atoh1-gfp (aka Math1-gfp), which is expressed in the dorsal most dI1 subpopulation of interneurons and their progenitors (Lumpkin et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The GFP+ neurons within the VZ are dorsal interneuron progenitors.
source: Our studies show that the GFP+ neurons within the VZ are dorsal interneuron progenitors
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The GFP+ neurons at the lateral spinal cord are differentiated interneurons.
source: and the ones at the lateral spinal cord are differentiated interneurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The GFP+ axons that fail to project to the midline are commissural axons.
source: In addition, the GFP+ axons that fail to project to the midline are commissural axons (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The GFP+ neuroprogenitors and interneurons express Dcc.
source: Furthermore, using fluorescent in situ hybridization, we found that the GFP+ neuroprogenitors and interneurons also express Dcc (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dcc is expressed in dorsal interneuron progenitors and interneurons.
source: consistent with previous reports that Dcc is expressed in these neuronal populations (Keino-Masu et al., 1996; Phan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nova deficiency appears to disturb commissural axon projection and also interferes with earlier stages of commissural neuron development in the progenitors.
source: Taken together, Nova deficiency appears to disturb commissural axon projection and also interferes with earlier stages of commissural neuron development in the progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data showing defects in both progenitors and axons.

claim: In WT embryos cultured for 20 hrs, many progenitors have reached the lateral spinal cord.
source: In WT embryos, we observed that many progenitors have reached the lateral spinal cord after 20 hrs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In both Nova and Dcc KOs cultured for 20 hrs, almost all GFP+ neurons are still positioned within the VZ.
source: However, in both Nova and Dcc KOs, almost all GFP+ neurons are still positioned within the VZ (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The increase in GFP+ neuroprogenitors in the VZ supports the idea that neuronal migration is reduced.
source: This supports the idea that neuronal migration is reduced.
evidence: This is an inference based on the migration tracking data.

claim: At E10.5, the number of neural stem cells and progenitors is normal in both Nova and Dcc mutants.
source: We found that at E10.5, the number of neural stem cells and progenitors is normal in both mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is no change in the localization or organization of SOX2+ and PAX3/7+ progenitor populations in Nova and Dcc mutants.
source: In addition, we labeled the neural progenitors in the whole spinal cord with SOX2 and the dorsal progenitors with PAX3/7, and found no change in the localization or organization of these progenitor populations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A normal number of interneurons are born in Nova and Dcc KOs at E10.5.
source: We also examined interneuron differentiation using the BARHL2, ISL1/2, and LHX5 markers, and found that a normal number of interneurons are born in Nova and Dcc KOs at E10.5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Figure 4).

claim: Both Nova and Dcc deficiency reduces neuroprogenitor migration, but does not affect cell proliferation or interneuron differentiation.
source: Therefore, both Nova and Dcc deficiency reduces neuroprogenitor migration, but does not affect cell proliferation or interneuron differentiation.

source: Barhl2 acts downstream of Atoh1 to specify the dI1 interneurons, including the dI1i (ipsilateral) and dI1c (commissural) populations (Ding et al., 2012; Figure 4A).

claim: DI1 neurons migrate both ventrally and laterally.
source: DI1 neurons migrate both ventrally and laterally

source: and dI1i migrates even further laterally than dI1c (Ding et al., 2012).

claim: Despite a transient delay in the migration, both commissural and ipsilateral neurons are properly specified in Nova and Dcc KOs.
source: Therefore, despite a transient delay in the migration, both commissural and ipsilateral neurons are properly specified.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the correct populations are present at E12.5.

claim: In the DSC assay, commissural axons extend out of the explant in the presence of Netrin-1 after a culture period of 16 hrs.
source: In this assay, commissural axons extend out of the explant in the presence of Netrin-1 after a culture period of 16 hrs (Serafini et al., 1994).

claim: Even after 24 hrs in the presence of Netrin-1, Nova dKO axons had very little growth.

claim: After 40 hrs of culturing in the absence of Netrin-1, there was robust axon outgrowth from both control and Nova dKO explants.

source: Rather, they fail to grow in response to Netrin stimulation.

claim: At E11.5, there are usually two main commissural axon bundles.
source: At E11.5, there are usually two main commissural axon bundles.

claim: Both commissural axon bundles are reduced in Nova dKOs and the more lateral one is more profoundly affected.
source: Both are reduced in Nova dKOs and the more lateral one is more profoundly affected.

claim: The size of the ventral commissure is reduced in Nova dKOs at E11.5.

claim: The severity of the axon guidance defect is similar between Nova and Dcc mutants.
source: The severity of the defect is similar between Nova and Dcc mutants (Figure 6).

source: One distinction between the two mutants is that Dcc KO axons are defasciculated and often invade the motor column (Xu et al., 2014)
